name: Alejandro Zumbado Vargas
title: Game & VR Developer
summary: Computer Engineer (TEC, 2019) passionate about game development, from competitive programming and game design competitions to shipped products. Experience with Unity/C# (2D and 3D), multiplayer networking (Netcode for GameObjects + Relay), XR for Meta Quest and XREAL, procedural level generation, and even Game Boy homebrew development. Currently at Opal Interactive building XR simulators and kiosk/AR apps for clients; in parallel I publish my own games and I'm packaging my own networking layer as a standalone product.

experience.sub: Studio that takes on projects from various companies and distributes them across its dev team
bullets: HealthSim: Unity XR training simulator (XREAL glasses) for medical laser equipment, with remote expert–trainee sessions via Netcode for GameObjects + Unity Relay.
totempanadol: Unity kiosk/AR app with thermal camera, face detection (ARFoundation), and QR code generation.
Additional VR/Unity projects for studio clients: a VR minigolf game and a BrissaNova brand activation.
Led end-to-end development of a VR-enabled website for the 'Doit' reconstruction project.
Designed and built 'Giz': an immersive nature experience with 5+ VR levels.
Built interactive web and VR experiences with A-Frame.js: editors, maps, and database-driven content.

projects.sub: 2–4 player FFA multiplayer · Unity 6000 · PC / Android / WebGL
bullets: Real-time color-matching combat game, playable at https://alejandrozumbado.github.io/tinted-showdown-build/.

Networking built with Netcode for GameObjects + Unity Relay; fixed 8+ real production issues (WebGL endpoint selection, decompression fallback, Multiplayer Play Mode safety, RPC serialization limits).

projects.sub: Drop-in join-code lobby system, preparing for release on Fab.com
bullets: Extracted the networking layer from Tinted Showdown and packaged it as a standalone UPM asset with its own docs, changelog, and license.
Fixes a WebGL-specific production bug (dynamic Relay endpoint selection) that silently breaks typical from-scratch implementations.
Tower-defense game with progression across up to 500 levels and custom editor tooling for level generation, playable at https://alejandrozumbado.github.io/cannons-build/.
Cross-platform support (PC mouse, Android touch) from a single codebase.
Python system that learns to play Cannons through self-play and uses what it learns to design new levels, running on GitHub Actions.
Battle royale game with a self-built Heroku backend and Photon multiplayer.
